chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about what the mine produces, whether little or much, is there any [zakat] in it? He said: 'There is no [zakat] in it until it reaches that which in similar cases zakat is twenty dinars.'

key_terms.عِشْرِينَ دِينَاراً: Twenty dinars (a specific currency value used as a threshold)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of minerals required to pay zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the nisab for minerals is based on their monetary value rather than weight, specifically equating it to twenty dinars (gold). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that treats mineral wealth similarly to gold and silver for zakat purposes, emphasizing the economic potential of the extracted resource. It provides a practical benchmark for calculating zakat on diverse mineral outputs, ensuring consistency with the broader principles of wealth purification in Shia jurisprudence.
